#comment: The following are CMOR internal settings and should not be edited by the user
comment: Complete native source grid retained without cropping or resampling; spatial extent 180°W–55°W, 15°N–80°N. These static products represent cumulative contemporary baseline soil organic carbon stocks generated by upscaling multi-decadal soil-profile observations with region-specific Random Forest models and environmental covariates. They are not temporal means or time series. The 0–30 cm and 0–100 cm cumulative intervals overlap and must not be summed.
contact: Zhuonan Wang (zzw0034@auburn.edu, zw5@ornl.gov); Jitendra Kumar (kumarj@ornl.gov); Debjani Sihi (dsihi@ncsu.edu)
geospatial_coverage: Original 30 arc-second rectangle: 180 W to 55 W, 15 N to 80 N; source mask retained
history: Original source raster values and masks retained; latitude and data rows reversed together; no time coordinate or spatial resampling; converted with CMOR.
license: Data in this file is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
references: Wang, Z., Kumar, J., Weintraub-Leff, S. R., Todd-Brown, K., Mishra, U., & Sihi, D. (2024). Upscaling soil organic carbon measurements at the continental scale using multivariate clustering analysis and machine learning. Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences, 129, e2023JG007702. https://doi.org/10.1029/2023JG007702
title: AI-upscaling 0-30 cm cSoil 1 (2024): Upscaling soil organic carbon measurements at the continental scale using multivariate clustering analysis and machine learning
variant_info: ORNL processing of two published cumulative SOC depth products. The depth interval is part of each source identity; the products are not ensemble members.
